These a_j strictly increase, and the count up to n is floor(n/M), giving density 1/M. Enumerate the complement on a density-zero schedule such as powers of two and L1 otherwise, always using the next unseen member. Both parts are infinite, so the stream is injective, complete, and vanishing-noisy for L1.
100: 
101: Core outputs satisfy `ceil(Mj)≤Mj+1≤Mn` once at least one complement output has occurred. Complement rank b_j grows at most linearly in j, while its scheduled time grows exponentially, so b_j≤Mn eventually. Relative to L1, rank j≤n≤Mn. Thus the exact required displacement holds for both targets. At M=1 take distinct cofinite L1=N\{1}, L2=N and the canonical stream; the upper bound one is immediate. Uniform correctness on both targets forces eventual containment in L1; for element outputs the finite initial exceptions do not change upper density.
